title: Primitive Recursiveness of the Fixed-Count Action Skipper
statement: For each fixed natural number $k$, the following partial reader is primitive recursive jointly in the bound $n$ and its Boolean-string input: it first consumes a pair of bits $(a,b)$ satisfying $a=1$ or $b=0$, then repeats $k$ times the operation of consuming any two bits followed by a pair satisfying that same condition, then consumes one more pair satisfying the condition, and finally consumes a state field. The state field is either a single $0$, or a $1$ followed by a unary numeral whose value is less than $n+1$; on success the reader returns the remaining suffix, and it fails if any required consumption is invalid or incomplete.
